title: Multiplayer parity sweep — port the post-S142 client-side rules (Throw Glove, Conveyor, Warp, Pressure Plate, Bomb Pass) into node-world-server
intent: Since S142 (Pierce) closed its server parity via GDP-027-002 / S147, five more rules shipped client-only with server parity explicitly OR implicitly deferred: S144 Throw Glove, S146 Conveyor Belt, S149 Warp Hole, S151 Pressure Plate, S152 Bomb Pass. In `connected` mode, anything not mirrored on the server creates a visible desync between client view (client sim) and authoritative state (server sim). Players currently see Bomb Pass / Throw Glove / belts / warps / plates work locally — but multiplayer interactions involving these rules are silently broken. This story is the consolidating sweep that closes ALL five defers in one focused parity pass. After this lands, every shipped client-side mechanic has its server twin and connected mode is correctness-complete.
rationale: Source: explicit defer notes in S144 + S152 sprint records + implicit defer (no server work shipped) in S146 + S149 + S151. Pattern set by S147 (Pierce server parity) — same shape: mirror one branch in node-world-server's matching system, add a parity test, document. Marked `should` because connected-mode players are functionally affected — solo unaffected. Consolidating into one story (vs 5 separate) keeps the parity sweep coherent: shared test harness, shared protocol field audit, one PR with all the deltas visible together.
acceptanceHints: Approach: ONE story, but dev may scope-down to a focused subset if a single sprint can't hold all 5. Recommended scoping: ship 3-of-5 per sprint MAX (smaller stories isolate failure modes). The 5 items below are listed in priority order — top 3 are highest-impact.
PRIORITY 1 — BOMB PASS (S152) — affects basic movement:

examples/backends/node-world-server: mirror the bomb-block-system from S152 in the server's grid-movement pipeline. Own bomb post-step-off is solid for placer UNLESS BomberStats.bombPass=true; other bombers' bombs always solid.
Server validates inputIntent against the bomb-block rule before applying. Client predicts; server reconciles.
Parity test: 2 tabs, tab A places bomb, tries to walk back over it — without bomb-pass, server denies the move (reconciliation snaps client back); with bomb-pass, server allows.
PRIORITY 2 — THROW GLOVE (S144) — affects bomb lifecycle:

examples/backends/node-world-server: mirror bomb-pickup-system + bomb-throw-system. Server validates PickupBombRequest (bomber owns bomb + on its cell + canThrow=true), pauses fuse on carried bombs, schedules a server-side timer for the throw arc landing.
Protocol: PickupBombRequest + ThrowBombRequest already exist client-side; server processes them server-authoritative.
Parity test: tab A bomber picks up + throws bomb 3 cells, tab B sees the bomb tween + land + fuse resume at the right cell.
PRIORITY 3 — CONVEYOR + WARP + PRESSURE PLATE (S146 + S149 + S151) — hazard modules:
All three currently run client-side only. In connected mode, the server's authoritative GridPosition doesn't account for belt-pushes / warp-teleports / plate-triggered bomb spawns.
Mirror each system in node-world-server's tick loop:
Conveyor: per fixedUpdate, push entities on belt cells (deterministic by entity-id order on contention).
Warp: instant teleport with 300ms per-pair cooldown.
Pressure Plate: spawn-bomb action triggers from server (S151 shipped only spawn-bomb; the other two action types are still deferred client-side per S151 notes).
Server snapshot reflects all three; client interpolator handles the position jumps (warp teleports are >1 cell delta → existing snap-not-smooth rule).
Parity test (one per hazard): two-tab playtest with hazard active → both tabs see consistent gameplay outcomes.
AUTHORING — minimal effort per port:

Each mirrored system shares ~80-90% of the client-side code. Where deterministic, extract the rule into a shared module (e.g. examples/kaboom-crew/src/rules/ → consumed by both client and server). This is the right time to factor.
S147 (Pierce server parity) showed that extracting the propagation rule into a shared module made the parity trivial. Apply the same approach to the 5 mirrored systems.
PROTOCOL AUDIT:
Verify each shipped feature's protocol message + snapshot fields are present:
Bomb Pass: BomberStats.bombPass already in snapshot.
Throw Glove: BomberStats.canThrow, Bomb.airborne, Bomb.carriedBy all in snapshot? Verify; if any missing, add to schema.
Hazards: ConveyorBelt + WarpHole + PressurePlate components in snapshot? Verify; the scene entities should already round-trip through the existing scene-snapshot.
No new protocol messages expected — the rules act on existing entity components.
DETERMINISM:

All five rules already deterministic client-side (no Math.random, no wall-clock-only sources). Server-side mirrors maintain determinism by using the server's tick clock + the server's seeded RNG (already in use for pickup drops).
Bot-vs-bot regression continues to resolve on the server-side world; visual replay may differ between tabs but gameplay state is identical.
ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST:
Two tabs join /?project=kaboom-crew&world=test&profile=connected with each tab controlling a bomber.
Test each rule:
Bomb Pass — tab A places bomb, walks back over it with bombPass — tab B sees the walk-through.
Throw Glove — tab A picks up + throws bomb — tab B sees the arc + landing + fuse resume.
Conveyor — both tabs see entities push along the belt in lockstep.
Warp — both tabs see teleport with no desync.
Pressure Plate — both tabs see spawn-bomb fire when the plate is touched.

DEFERRABILITY: if dev capacity is tight, the priority order is firm — Bomb Pass (basic movement) first, then Throw Glove (lifecycle), then hazards. A partial ship is acceptable; the remaining items stay in the next sprint's plan.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Pressure Plate v2 actions (open-gate + arena-event) — those defer from S151 client-side first; server parity follows after those land client-side.
Bot-AI awareness of any hazard (Conveyor / Warp / Plate). Bots treat hazards as neutral travel cost per existing decisions.
Snapshot relevance filter (server only sends nearby entities). Current 15×11 arena fits whole snapshot; filter is a separate optimisation story.
Lag compensation / hit rewind. No hitscan in this game; bombs are slow-fuse, lag tolerable.
